verdict: Lend selectively to Lucknow hospital and diagnostics operators with verified payer mix and doctor retention; the data pack gives no score, so the call rests on first principles and peer evidence, and public-sector digitalisation news is not a credit signal.
title: Lucknow Hospitals & Diagnostics: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A hospital turns doctors, beds, OT time and diagnostic machines into billed episodes; a diagnostics lab turns collection centres, technicians and machines into tests. **Cash arrives at the point of service, but value sits in occupancy, test volumes per patient and doctor loyalty.** Peer data shows the model: 22 lakh tests and 3.8 lakh patients in a quarter, 5.8 tests per patient, average revenue per test Rs 357 and per patient Rs 2,083 [7]. So when a proposal lands, check tests per patient and revenue per patient against these peer marks; if revenue per test is falling while volumes rise, ask whether discounting or a payer-mix shift is driving it.

## Where cash and value sit
**Hospitals carry heavy fixed cost and re-investment needs, so cash is made on occupancy and payer mix, not on list price.** ICRA notes hospitals have significant re-investment requirements for expansion and upgradation of facilities [9]. Peer Aster reported operating EBITDA of Rs 253 crore at a 21.7 percent margin, up from 19.3 percent, on volume growth and operating leverage [5]. So when a proposal lands, check the EBITDA margin and whether it comes from volume or from cost cuts; if margin expansion is claimed without volume growth, ask for department-wise occupancy and payer mix. Collect from customer: bed occupancy, ALOS, share of cash versus insurance and government schemes, and debtor days by payer.

## What has changed now
**The local news is about public hospitals going digital, not about private demand.** RSM Hospital is fully digital with 10 online services [2], five OPD registration counters and 40 computers [3], and Civil Hospital performed a complex endoscopic brain tumour surgery [1]. These show public capacity improving, which pressures private players on routine work. Peer commentary says diagnostics demand and pricing are stable into FY27 [4][6], but one peer's average revenue per test fell 8.7 percent year on year even as tests rose 29.2 percent [7] — volume growth with price softness. Rating reports flag intense competition from organised chains and mid-sized hospitals, with doctor retention critical [10], and regulatory risk for hospital chains [11]. The ICRA merger note is dated December 2024 and is old [8].

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue diagnostics-led and single-specialty operators with dense collection networks and private-pay mix; avoid greenfield multi-specialty hospitals with unproven doctor teams.** Structure term loans to capex milestones with a moratorium matched to ramp-up, and working capital against verified receivables, not projected billing. Take monthly: collection-centre-wise test volumes, payer-wise receivables ageing, doctor attrition list, and machine utilisation.

## Early-warning signs
- **Falling revenue per test with rising volumes** [7]: check discounting and payer mix monthly; if it persists two quarters, cut exposure. - **Doctor exits or department closures** [10]: get the attrition list monthly; if a key specialist leaves, ask for the replacement contract before the next disbursement. - **Margin built on cost cuts rather than volume** [5]: review department-wise occupancy quarterly; if occupancy is flat, treat margin claims as unproven.
